title: SLO Root-Cause Orchestration and Mentor-Guided Handover
author: Grace Li
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines an operational pattern we use when an SLO deviation surfaces that requires deeper root-cause orchestration AND a human-to-human handover between the first responder and a mentor/subject-matter-owner. It blends incident containment steps with an educational, audit-friendly handover checklist to accelerate time-to-resolution and to increase responder capability over time.

Scope
- Applies to any SLO breach labeled P0 or P1 against the following services: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache-service, batching-engine, and attribution-logger.
- Not for scheduled maintenance or planned capacity change events (use the maintenance playbook).

Signal thresholds and severity mapping
| Signal | Threshold | Severity |
|---|---:|---|
| 99th pct latency (inference-gateway) | > 500ms for 5m window | P1 |
| Error rate (model-router 5xx) | > 5% for 3m window | P0 |
| KV cache miss storm | > 80% miss for 10m | P1 |
| Token generation stalls (batching-engine) | > 30s median step times | P0 |

Roles and quick ownership
- First Responder (FR): individual on primary on-call; owns initial evidence capture and immediate containment.
- Mentor / SME: senior engineer (rotated roster) tasked with guided handover and root cause deep-dive facilitation.
- Bridge Operator: communications lead who posts status updates and organizes cross-team bridge.
- Recorder: documents timeline and artifacts for postmortem.

Quick containment checklist (FR, executed within first 10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge page and set bridge: /run bridge create --service inference-gateway --priority P1
2) Collect evidence snapshot: logs, pprof, tracer links, and current SLO dashboard snapshot. Use these commands:
   - kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-gateway --since=15m | gzip > /tmp/inf-gw-logs.gz
   - curl -sS "https://obs.company.internal/api/traces?service=inference-gateway&window=15m" > /tmp/traces.json
3) Apply short-lived mitigation (if applicable): scale up inference-gateway by +2 pods, enable degraded-mode routing: curl -XPOST https://control-plane/configs/routing -d '{"mode":"degraded","map":[{"from":"*","to":"fallback-small-model"}]}'
4) Notify Bridge Operator with initial impact assessment and ask for SME/mentor coverage within next 5–10 minutes.

Mentor-guided handover: handshake protocol (FR -> Mentor)
- When to handover: FR should request mentor if the incident meets any of: multi-region impact, sustained SLO violation > 15 mins, or requires cross-team coordination (networking, infra, model ops).
- Handover steps (use numbered checklist while on the bridge):
  1. FR reads a 2–3 sentence summary: "What happened, when it started, what is currently mitigated."
  2. FR shares artifacts: dashboard links, sample request IDs, error snippets, and mitigation commands executed.
  3. Mentor performs rapid hypothesis triage (3–5 minutes) and proposes next experiment.
  4. If Mentor requires a deeper investigation, FR transitions to Recorder and leaves a documented open action list with assumed-owners.

Handover checklist (to be checked live on the bridge)
- [ ] Evidence snapshot link (dashboard, logs, traces) present in bridge notes.
- [ ] List of mitigation steps already executed with timestamps.
- [ ] Active customer-impact statement (what features are affected and user-visible behavior).
- [ ] Named SME and agreed next steps with ETA.

Decision ladder for exercise of rollbacks and fallbacks
1) If a recent model release coincides with regression signal: consider immediate pin to previous model (model-router pin command):
   curl -XPOST https://ops.api/models/pin -d '{"service":"inference","model":"v2026-02-05","duration_minutes":60}'
2) If KV cache miss storm: enable read-through caching fallback for 20 minutes and progressively key-scan hot-keys.
3) If tiered latency spike with noisy neighbor signature: apply tenant isolation policy and move heavy tenants to burst instances.

Bridge notes and customer status templates (use these verbatim as starting points)
- Internal bridge headline (short): "P1 — inference-gateway: increased 99th latency; working mitigations; SME engaged."
- Public status-page initial message (tiered):
  "We are investigating increased request latency for text-generation requests (service: inference-gateway) affecting some customers in us-west-2. We have engaged engineering, applied temporary mitigations and will provide updates every 15 minutes."
- Public status-page update (15–60m):
  "Mitigations applied: degraded routing to fallback models and scaled capacity. Error rates have stabilized but high latency persists for a subset of requests. Root-cause investigation ongoing."
- Customer-facing post-incident template (final):
  "Summary: On 2026-02-10 at 02:10 UTC, customers in us-west-2 experienced elevated latency for text generation due to a cascading cache eviction triggered during a model rollout. Impact: requests experienced higher 99th percentile latency and increased error rates for 14 minutes. Actions taken: we rolled back the model, scaled inference-gateway, and implemented a patch to cache eviction heuristics. Follow-ups: we will deploy a rolling patch, add regression alerts tied to model rollouts, and provide a code-level RCA in the postmortem."

Mentor development and knowledge transfer expectations
- Mentors should:
  - Shadow at least 2 FR handovers per quarter.
  - Provide a short 30-minute reflection within 48 hours with the FR covering: what went well, one improvement to the runbook, and one training task for the FR.
- FRs should:
  - Complete the handover checklist in the bridge notes before stepping back.
  - File an incident ticket with assigned Recorder and link artifacts within 2 hours.

Post-incident artifacts and timeline (minimum deliverables)
1) Evidence bundle (logs, traces, pprof, snapshot of SLO dashboard).
2) Timeline (UTC timestamps, actions, decision rationale).
3) Root cause summary (one paragraph + technical cause).
4) Remediation plan with owners and ETA.
5) Regression tests to prevent recurrence and a rollout gating checklist for model releases if relevant.

Example minimal timeline table (text)
| Time (UTC) | Actor | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 02:08 | Alerting | 99th latency > 500ms detected |
| 02:09 | FR | Page acknowledged, bridge created |
| 02:12 | FR | Scaled inference-gateway +2 pods |
| 02:17 | Mentor | Joined bridge, suggested degraded routing |
| 02:29 | Ops | Model pinned to v2026-02-05 |
| 02:40 | Bridge | Public status update posted |
| 02:54 | SRE | Latency back within SLO (99th < 500ms) |

Operational KPIs this pattern targets
- Mean time to containment (MTTC): target < 15 minutes for P1.
- Mean time to mentor handover: target < 12 minutes when requested.
- Time to customer-visible resolution (SLO restored): target < 60 minutes for P1.

Runbook governance and review cadence
- This document and related handover checklists are reviewed quarterly by the incident council.
- Any incident invoking a mentor handover must be included in the mentor training log and used as a scenario in the next game day.

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- Copy of SLO dashboard: https://dash.company.internal/slo/inference-gateway
- Create bridge (internal CLI): /run bridge create --service <service> --priority <P0|P1>
- Evidence collection helper (script): /ops/scripts/collect-incident-bundle.sh inference-gateway 15m /tmp/incident-{{TIMESTAMP}}

Revision history
- 2026-02-10: Initial published (Grace Li).
- 2026-03-01: Added mentor training expectations and updated severity thresholds (reviewers: Marcus Chen, Aisha Patel).
